main_text.p: non collabascat, concutiatur saltem. Si itaque hic oculus tenebrosus fit,certè magnæ, necesse est, sint tenebræ totins corporis: tamen satiùs puto, ut judicio divino reservetur, quàm cum totius corporis periculo evellatur,ne ipso morbo deterius remedium inveniatur. Ad. Chyrographum cœleste redeo: {r}Dijs non detrahes, & Principi populi tui non maledices, inquit Dominus per Mo-senExod. 22.; & per Davidem, {f}Nolite tangere Christos meos: & per Salomonem,{t}In cogitatione tua Regine detrahas, qui & aves cœli portabunt vocem tuam, & qui habent pennas annuntiabunt sententiam: tantum abest, ut trucidare permittat,ut ne maledicere quidem, ne in secreto cubiculi, aut malitiosè tangere liceat. Memi-nit Marcus Cicero in {u}Oratione suaPsal. 104.Eccles. 10.Cicer[?] u[?] circa medium.pro Sexto Roscio Amerino, Romanos, Cùm intelligerent nihil esse tam sanctum, quod non aliquando violaret audacia, supplicium in parricidas singulare excogitasse: ut quos natura ipsa retinere in officio non potuissent, ij magnitudine poenae maleficio summoverentur, insui voluerunt in culeam vivos

page.notes: The first word "collabascat" carries a cedilla-like mark over the c in the scan; read as printed. The bottom left margin note is cut at the edge of the scan and only its first letters are visible. The reference marks in the text (r, f, t, u) match the margin notes. Scan shows stains and faint marks in the left margin; not transcribed. The marginal note's first word is cut at the top of the scan and was read as "u" with [?]. "natura" carries a doubtful accent over the a, transcribed without it. A stray mark stands above "Amerino" in the italic name and is not transcribed. The catchword "atque" sits right-aligned under the last full line, above the ruled rule.
